page.text: The NTgCalls Client is your primary interface for interacting with Telegram Calls. This page covers what surrounds the API: how to create and dispose of an instance, how to read the library version, and how to route the library logs into your own logging setup. Everything else is documented in the Reference section.

subtext.text: The instance owns every connection you open through it. It is released by the garbage collector, and every call it still holds is stopped at interpreter exit, so there is nothing to dispose of by hand.
Version of the native library the bindings were built against.
Creates an instance and returns the handle every other function takes as its first argument. The handle is yours to release.
Stops every call still open on the handle and frees it.
Version of the native library. The returned string is owned by the library.
Message of the last failure on the calling thread. Every function returns an ntg_result code, and this is where the detail behind it lives.
The instance owns every connection you open through it and is released by the garbage collector, so there is nothing to dispose of by hand.
The constructor loads the native library and allocates the instance. The native side is released when the object is finalized, so there is nothing to dispose of by hand.
The instance owns every connection you open through it and releases the native side on Drop, so there is nothing to dispose of by hand.

page.text: The library reports its own diagnostics and the ones coming from WebRTC. How they reach you depends on the binding.

lang-block.text: The logs are routed into the standard logging module, under the ntgcalls and webrtc loggers. Both are set to CRITICAL on import unless your application has already given them a level, so claim them before creating the instance to see anything.
Install a callback to receive every message, along with its level, source, file and line. Passing NULL stops the delivery.
The logs go to the console. Pick how much of them you want with setLogLevel, which accepts a value of the LogLevel enum.
The logs go to the Android system log, under the ntgcalls tag.
The logs are forwarded to the log crate, on the ntgcalls and ntgcalls::webrtc targets, so any logger implementation picks them up.

page.text: Every callback is registered on the instance and documented, one page each, in the Callbacks section of the Reference.
